**Yes — the numbers add up exactly for the study the text cites.**

- The text (p. 2) states: "A pan-genome analysis of 45 isolates revealed 19,469 total genes, of which only 3155 (~16.2%) are core genes" (ref. [44], Abreo & Altier, *Sci. Rep.* 2019 — p. 14 of the reference list).
- Fig. 2E (p. 4) plots this dataset under "Eduardo et al. 2019" with three bars: core (>95%) = 3155, dispensable = 7847, unique = 8467. These sum to 19,469, matching the stated total, and 3155/19,469 = 16.2%, matching the stated percentage.

Two caveats:

1. Fig. 2E also shows two other pan-genome datasets for which the text gives no totals: "Danesh et al. 2016" (core >99% = 3372; soft core = 342; shell = 1526; cloud = 8347) and "Filipe et al. 2018" (core 100% = 2107; accessory = 7656; unique = 6693). These sum to 13,587 and 16,456 respectively, i.e. they differ from 19,469, but the text only describes them generally as showing "extensive genomic diversity within the species" (p. 2, refs [45,46]), so there is no numerical conflict.
2. The figure labels the Abreo & Altier dataset as "Eduardo et al. 2019" (first name rather than surname), a citation-style inconsistency with reference [44], but the gene counts themselves are consistent.
